The first time Yi Dao met the little one of Han Xiangxun, he scoffed.
Where did this clueless kid come from?
Not only did the kid not run when he saw the infamous Killerblade, but he even dared to draw his own sword.
Gutsy, Yi Dao thought. But let's see how long those guts last against a few of my swings.
They fought, with blade against blade. The kid was no match for him, but when Yi Dao struck, there was no blood. The kid stared at him in shock. Yi Dao had used the back of his blade.
He realized then that this laughably clumsy swordplay was familiar.
So Han Xiangxun raised a kid this naive? She was never an easy one herself.
The kid seemed to know all sorts of people. The kid might be more useful alive than dead. Still, he needed to teach the kid a lesson that Jianghu was a dangerous place.
Yi Dao sheathed his blade.
"Hey, take me to Blissful Retreat."

Just showing the way, there is no need to be so cagey about it.
As soon as he went ahead to scout, the little kid predictably slipped away at the first chance.
Yi Dao always kept his word. If he said he wouldn't kill, then he wouldn't kill.
And yet, the kid still didn't trust him. Did he really think Yi Dao would go looking for trouble with Han Xiangxun, that troublesome woman?
But honestly, a kid who's barely out of childhood, even with some wits, was no match for a seasoned old hand like Yi Dao.
In the thick fog, Yi Dao called out half-heartedly, then swaggered after the panicked, fleeing figure ahead.
Seriously, as if anyone could escape the Killerblade unless he let them!
He couldn't help but grin smugly.
Run, kid, run! The faster you go, the more you're giving your Aunt Han away!

In his youth, he apprenticed under Old Man Xue, mastering miraculous arts: treading on fire and blades, transplanting melons and wells, conjuring clouds and mists at will, and shaping mountains and rivers from thin air—feats that left onlookers in awe. Chou was renowned for his cunning. He assisted Ghostlight Market Elder and Dao Lord Zhu Yousheng in founding the Nine Mortal Ways to resist the Khitan forces, winning great prestige among the people for his strategic acumen.
After Zhu Yousheng's death and as his disciples came of age, Xue Chou retired to oversee the Oil Umbrella faction. He often performed illusionary acts in the Fairgrounds, gaining renown for his craft. When envoys from various states converged on the capital, the Emperor wished to stage a performance to showcase imperial might and entrusted the task to Chou.
If later generations of jianghu practitioners are destined to meet him, they may seek his trace at the Beast Reverie Stage in the Fairgrounds—perhaps they will find what they seek.

Thirteen years ago, in the Dingwei year, during a time of chaos, the Khitan army invaded Kaifeng, unleashing fire and slaughter. The people rose to defend their homes, and after a month of bitter fighting, the invaders were repelled. As the city rebuilt, an old tree in the northwest was found scorched by the fires of war, yet miraculously sprouting new leaves. Seeing it as a divine sign of resilience, the people named it the Immortal Tree.
Later, when the usurper Liu Zhiyuan founded his short-lived Han dynasty, his sycophantic court seized upon this story. Claiming the tree as a heavenly omen, they forcibly expelled the local residents and built the Garden of Auspicious Omen, adorning its burnt branches with paper flowers to flatter their emperor.
And yet, what came of it? The Liu Han dynasty collapsed in just two generations. A dynasty's fate is not bound to trinkets and omens. How can a ruler in troubled times dare to cast aside caution for arrogance?
Now, in the first year of Jianlong, with the founding of the Great Song, the realm remains divided. Our Emperor, taking this tale of hubris as a solemn warning, has decreed that the garden be remade. It is renamed the Garden of Vigilance and returned to the people, a testament to his vow to rule with virtue, to remain ever-cautious, and to protect the nation and its people.
Decreed and erected in the seventh month of the first year of the Jianlong era
